why: What each consultant runtime can and cannot be kept from doing, per platform, in a sentence a person reads
under the consultant's row (the Consultant tab, and coai-mcp --consultants). Requirement 12 of
PLAN_the_consultant_works_on_every_vendor.md: a limitation never claims more than was measured. So every
row carries EITHER `measured` (date, CLI version, the cells, the document that records them) OR `source`
(a sentence saying it was not measured here and why we believe what the row says) - never neither.
One row per runtime x platform (windows | linux | wsl | macos), and for claude also per capability:
`restricted` when the installed CLI declares --restricted, `no-restricted` when it does not
(ClaudeCapability reads it off `claude --help` before every launch). No platform inherits another's row:
a platform nobody measured gets an `unmeasured` row of its own, and a platform this file does not name at
all is answered `unmeasured` by the lookup, never with the nearest platform's text.
`standing` is one of: confined (cannot read outside the repository), unconfined (can), default-deny (the
CLI refuses what it would have to ask a person about), unmeasured.
antigravity rows also carry `settingsPath` (where agy reads permissions.allow on that side) and, on

linux/wsl ONLY, `snippet`: a permissions.allow rule measured to work there (research/RESULTS_agy_allow_rule.md), always with its `snippetWarning` (the loader refuses one without the other, or either off linux/wsl).
On Windows agy honoured only exact command lines, so no snippet is offered. coai never writes agy's settings.
Embedded in coai-mcp (CoaiMcp.Runners) and read through a source-generated JSON context; the extension
